name: What Do Garage Addition Estimates Commonly Miss?

mainEntity.name: What garage addition features are most often missing from contractor estimates in Los Angeles County?
mainEntity.text: What garage addition features are most often missing from contractor estimates in Los Angeles County?

acceptedAnswer.text: Homeowners are often surprised when the final bill includes items that were not obvious in the original estimate. For garage additions, the most commonly missed costs are permits, engineering, grading, drainage, utility trenching, electrical panel upgrades, insulation, drywall, interior finish work, and exterior patching or cleanup. Some contractors also exclude demolition, disposal, or driveway restoration. In Los Angeles County, these omissions matter because even a simple garage can involve several specialized trades and local compliance steps. The best defense is to ask for an estimate that separates base construction from optional upgrades and clearly labels exclusions. If an estimate is unusually short or vague, it may be leaving out the most expensive parts of the job. Homeowners should insist on written clarification before signing so they can compare bids accurately and avoid surprise change orders.
acceptedAnswer.description: Commonly missed items include permit fees, engineering, grading, drainage, electrical upgrades, insulation, drywall, paint, and final cleanup. Some estimates also omit site access costs, utility trenching, or finish upgrades that become necessary later.
